# Vendored kimi-cli wire fixture

`wire.jsonl` is vendored byte-identical from the official MoonshotAI/kimi-code
repository, which is MIT licensed:

- Upstream: `packages/migration-legacy/test/fixtures/large-100msgs/wire.jsonl`
  at `main` (https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code)
- Local copy: 130 lines, 15 usage-bearing `StatusUpdate` records whose
  `token_usage` objects use exactly the vendor wire keys `input_other`,
  `output`, `input_cache_read`, `input_cache_creation`
- sha256: `2611f26f4bbfa92602b4bcd5513845c1141bfa34d3526314350c510577272d13`

It is the golden corpus for the rm-400 kimi_cli usage-alias test
(`kimi_statusupdate_usage_uses_official_wire_aliases` in
`crates/agenttrace-core/src/parser.rs`): the shared usage-alias table must
keep matching the vendor's real wire keys so the reported totals
(62,198 input / 4,790 output / 496,640 cache read / 0 cache write =
563,628) survive instead of collapsing to the text estimator's 132. Every
alias match is disclosed per session as `kimi_usage_alias:<key>`
counters on the non-loss disclosure channel (rm-719: "Disclosed facts",
not parse loss), so a future vendor key change surfaces as nonzero
counters rather than silently-zero usage.

Do not edit this file. To refresh, re-fetch the upstream fixture, confirm
the record census (15 usage-bearing `StatusUpdate` records, the four wire
keys only), and update the sha256 above — a mismatch means the golden
corpus has drifted and the pinned test totals must be re-measured, not
transcribed.
